name: Connors RSI(2) mean reversion (MA-trend-filtered) (Pine import)
rationale: Faithful import of Larry Connors' RSI(2) system (Connors & Alvarez, 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work'; the canonical TradingView/Pine community port: long only when close is above the 200-period MA, enter when a very-short RSI drops into a deep-oversold extreme, exit when RSI snaps back above a high level). Economic mechanism: inside an established uptrend (price above its long MA), a sharp 2-day RSI washout is a short-term liquidity/overreaction dip — forced or panicked selling that overshoots — and price reverts to the prevailing trend once the flush exhausts. The long-MA filter is load-bearing: it restricts dip-buying to assets that are structurally trending up, so 'oversold' is a pullback to be bought rather than the start of a downtrend (the classic 'falling knife' that an unfiltered RSI(2) catches). The defining, distinct structural piece vs our other reversion specs is the MaTrendFilter (setup.ma_trend_filter) — a fitted long-MA regime gate — paired with a very SHORT RSI lookback pushed to a deep-oversold floor (Connors used RSI(2) < 5-10, far more extreme than a generic RSI(14)<30 dip) and an RSI-normalization signal exit (Connors exits the snap-back, he does not run to a target). Translation losses (noted, not fabricated): (1) Connors deliberately used NO hard stop (he found stops hurt index mean-reversion); we ADD a fitted stop_loss + time_stop purely as a risk disconfirmer so a regime break is bounded — this is a deliberate, conservative deviation from the source, not the source's rule; (2) the RSI period is a fitted lookback the Finder pins toward the very-short Connors regime; (3) the 200-MA is a fitted ma_lookback. Honest prior: RSI(2) is a heavily-published equity-index edge; on crypto spot net of ~20bps it is far less established and may not survive — expected a powered fail/marginal that maps the deep-reversion surface; the Gate disposes. Disconfirmer: the RSI-snap-back signal exit fires when the dip is bought (thesis realized); the stop + time-stop close a dip that keeps falling (thesis wrong — the uptrend was breaking).
catalyst: deep 2-period RSI washout while price remains above its long-MA uptrend
